description: Complete weather overview for a location: current conditions, daily forecast (SPC threats, severity; view "detailed" adds CAPE, UV, full day/night periods), active alerts, and outlooks in one call. Pre-aggregated across NBM, HRRR, GFS, RTMA, and SPC and unit-converted server-side. Primary weather tool; reach for lower-level tools only when you need raw observations or a specific dataset. Times are UTC ISO 8601; quote daily[].astro.local to users, not UTC. If forecast.location.timezone_resolved is false, zone unknown: state times as UTC, never as local. Accepts a place name directly. Examples: {"location": "Denver, CO"} or {"location": "Portland, OR", "days": 5} or {"lat": 41.4, "lon": -92.9}.

include.description: Comma-separated sections: current, daily, hourly, alerts, outlooks. Default "current,daily,alerts,outlooks". Use get_hourly_forecast for hourly detail.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

units.description: Units of every value in and out: imperial (default; °F, mph, in) or metric (°C, km/h, mm). si is deprecated and will be removed; use metric.

view.description: concise (default; REST's is detailed), ~5-10KB: daily has day_precip_probability / night_precip_probability (precip_probability is their max). detailed, ~12-20KB: adds CAPE, UV, full day/night periods, extra hourly fields.

name: get_forecast

data_status.description: Present only when the platform reports degraded/outage data sources: overall state, a caveat note, and the affected sources. Absent means no advisory was available -- not a freshness guarantee. See get_platform_status for the full document.

widget.description: sw-ui-spec widget block rendered by the MCP Apps weather widget (ui://weather-widget/v1/index.html). Additive; safe to ignore.
